PurposeFounder-level command matrix for deciding which review layer must lead a live issue, which supporting controls must be linked, and what output is required before approval, executable movement, escalation, or containment.

Founder usePut every urgent issue into the right control room before urgency, chat, or partial evidence creates a shortcut.
Protection ruleThis dashboard governs routing only; approved templates, brand assets, and source-record protections stay unchanged.

Control Routing PostureLink

Control lensCurrent postureFounder readRequired response
Routing clarityLead layers are mostly named, but live issues can still touch several boards at once.The system has depth; the next risk is using the wrong layer first.Declare one lead control before any founder decision is treated as executable.
Urgency pressureRelease, payment, trust, and exception issues can still invite chat-first shortcuts.Same-day urgency should trigger tighter routing, not looser documentation.Route urgent movement through executable-check, funding, release, or scenario boards before widening.
Cross-functional complexityAtlantic Foods still links pricing, trust, release, claim, CAPA, and exception logic.A single matter can fragment founder attention if routing is not explicit.Use matter control and exception governance whenever one account accumulates multiple deviations.
Decision readinessControl integrity now sits between strategic alignment and execution.A synced story is not automatically executable.Require integrity and executable-check proof before movement leaves the board.
Founder bandwidthRepeated founder calls reveal routing or ownership weakness.Founder attention should be scarce and decision-ready, not used as the glue between records.Convert repeated misroutes into owner accountability, adoption drift, or plan variance.

Same-Day Routing SequenceLink

Sequence stepRequired answerLead recordStop condition
Identify movement typeIs the request pricing, payment, release, trust, claim, CAPA, owner, plan, or scenario movement?06_dashboard/33_control-routing/Founder-Control-Routing-Matrix.mdStop if the movement type is unclear.
Select lead controlWhich board owns the next decision before any supporting context is discussed?06_dashboard/33_control-routing/Founder-Control-Routing-Matrix.mdStop if two boards are competing without a named lead.
Verify source freshnessAre linked inputs current enough to trust?06_dashboard/34_control-integrity/Executive-Control-Integrity-and-Decision-Readiness-Review.mdStop if source records are stale, conflicting, or missing.
Confirm executable statusIs the next move executable, not executable, contained, or blocked?06_dashboard/40_executable-checks/Trust-Override-Executable-Check-Control-Board.mdStop if trust-linked movement lacks executable-check proof.
Record founder decisionWhat is approved, blocked, expired, escalated, or returned to standard?06_dashboard/13_founder-decisions/Executive-Decision-Board.mdStop if the decision lacks owner, output, or blocked-action language.

Routing Stop RulesLink

Stop ruleConditionRequired escalationFounder action
No lead-control stopIssue has more than one plausible board and no declared lead.Route to this matrix and matter control.Pause decision until the lead layer is named.
Stale-input stopSupporting records are stale, conflicting, or incomplete.Route to control integrity.Do not approve from partial truth.
Executable ambiguity stopTrust-linked movement is requested without executable or not-executable status.Route to executable-check board.Block movement until status is explicit.
Exception ambiguity stopOverride is requested without expiry, blocked action, or return-to-standard language.Route to exception governance and founder decisions.Tighten or reject the override.
Founder-rescue repeatSame issue returns to founder because routing or owner behavior failed.Route to owner accountability, adoption readiness, and plan variance as relevant.Treat as system-use failure, not routine escalation.
